title: Arthashastra
author: kautilya
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Kautilya, also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta. The surviving text is composite and its date and single authorship are disputed; the attribution is recorded, not adjudicated.
description: A Sanskrit treatise on government, economy, law, war and intelligence, in fifteen books. It ranges from the duties of the king and the organisation of villages to taxation, trade, diplomacy, fortification and the conduct of war. Shamasastry's 1915 translation made the text widely available in English.
historicalContext: The Arthashastra is a composite Sanskrit treatise of the Mauryan or post-Mauryan period, rediscovered in a manuscript in 1904 and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909 and 1915. It is a historical treatise on statecraft, not a universally binding code.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Wikisource page by page at read time. The fifteen books are complete for the Shamasastry translation. The translation is a historical scholarly rendering, not a modern critical edition.
